title: Dense operations dashboard, no toolchain
prompt:
Create a single self-contained index.html file (inline CSS, no build step, no dependencies, no JavaScript libraries) for an internal operations dashboard.

Heading: "Northwind Logistics" with the subtitle "Q3 2026 Operations Review".

A row of four KPI tiles, each showing the figure and its change against last quarter:
  On-time delivery  94.2%  (+1.8 pts)
  Average transit   3.4 days  (-0.2 days)
  Cost per shipment $18.40  (+$0.60)
  Damage rate       0.7%  (-0.1 pts)

A depot table with one row per depot and four columns -- Depot, Shipments, On-time, Cost/shipment:
  Rotterdam   48,210   96.1%   $16.20
  Hamburg     41,930   95.4%   $17.05
  Antwerp     37,480   93.8%   $17.80
  Gdansk      22,150   92.2%   $19.40
  Lyon        19,870   94.7%   $18.10
  Milan       18,640   91.5%   $20.30
  Valencia    16,220   90.8%   $21.15
  Bristol     14,090   95.9%   $17.60
  Gothenburg  11,360   97.3%   $16.85
  Tallinn      8,740   89.4%   $22.40

Below the table, a "Top five by volume" section listing Rotterdam, Hamburg, Antwerp, Gdansk and Lyon with a horizontal bar beside each, drawn in CSS, whose length is proportional to that depot's shipment count.

A footer reading "Prepared by the Operations Desk".

Make it look like a dashboard someone would actually put on a wall: aligned numeric columns, a clear type hierarchy, deliberate spacing.

rubric.description: The page shows a real interface, not a blank page, a loading spinner, or an error overlay.
A heading reading "Northwind Logistics" is visible, with "Q3 2026 Operations Review" as a subtitle near it.
Four KPI tiles are laid out in a row, each showing a figure and its change against last quarter (for example 94.2% with +1.8 pts).
A depot table is visible with at least ten data rows and four columns: depot name, shipments, on-time percentage, and cost per shipment.
The table's figures are correct where they can be read: the Rotterdam row shows 48,210 and 96.1% and $16.20, and the Tallinn row shows 8,740 and 89.4% and $22.40.

A "Top five by volume" section is visible, and each of the five depots has a horizontal bar beside it whose length is clearly proportional to its shipment count -- Rotterdam's bar is the longest and Lyon's the shortest.
A footer reading "Prepared by the Operations Desk" is visible.
The table's numeric columns are aligned as a column of numbers rather than ragged left-aligned text, so the figures can be scanned down the page.
It reads as a deliberately designed dashboard -- consistent type scale, considered spacing, visual separation between the KPI row, the table and the chart -- rather than stacked unstyled HTML.

iterations.description: The canonical small visual edit, with no bundler in the loop.
iterations.check: (() => { const h = document.querySelector('h1') || document.querySelector('h2'); if (!h) return false; const m = getComputedStyle(h).color.match(/\d+/g); if (!m) return false; const [r,g,b] = m.map(Number); return b > 90 && b > r + 25 && b > g + 15; })()

iterations.prompt: Add an eleventh depot row for Porto: 6,480 shipments, 93.1% on-time, $19.95 cost per shipment.
iterations.description: A structural edit into the middle of a dense table, rather than a style token. Matched case-insensitively because innerText is the text as rendered.
